newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: NSW PREMIER SAYS 6000 JOBS IN PIPELINE PLAN
New South Wales Premier, Bob Carr, says a proposed 380 million dollar gas pipeline from Bass Strait to Wollongong has the potential to create 6000 new jobs.
Mr Carr says a Commission of Inquiry report on the 750-kilometre underground link has ruled that the project may proceed subject to environmental safeguards.
The inquiry report is now with Planning minister Craig Knowles who will assess it and advise Energy minister Michael Egan whether or not to approve the pipeline.
Mr Carr says a government analysis shows the project could boost the state economy by nearly two billion dollars and save Wollongong businesses 90-million dollar a year in power bills.
ALL TIME HIGH IN RURAL EXPORTS PREDICTED
New figures from the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics suggest an all-time-high in the value of rural exports for this financial year.
ABARE says a bumper winter wheat crop is predicted to be the second highest on record, with seven percent more wheat being planted than last year.
It says this will mean a fall in price, but predicts that cropping incomes will still be higher than they have been for many years.
ABARE's also forecasting a positive outlook for the minerals and energy sectors with export earnings expected to rise, but wool prices are expected to remain flat.
DALAI MEETS FEDERAL MPS IN CANBERRA
The Federal Opposition leader and the seven Australian Democrat senators have met with the Dalai Lama at Parliament House.
Democrats Senator Vicki Bourne says the exiled Tibetan spiritual leader appealed to the group to publicly support Tibet's push for autonomy from China.
Senator Borne says he didn't say that self-determination for Tibet ss necessary, but that the withdrawal of troops, and the cessation of human rights abuses and torture are.

She says the Democrats gave him a clear message of support for his attitude toward non-violent change and Tibet's autonomy. Meanwhile, the Government's Senate Leader, Robert Hill, says the Prime Minister who's in Asia on a week long tour, is likely to meet the Dalai Lama, subject to other commitments.
TELSTRA TO REFUND A$45 MILLION
Communications giant Telstra has admitted it didn't give customers the information they needed about services which were changed in 1989.
This follows an investigation by the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission.
The finding forces Telstra to make a 45-million dollar compensation payout, in the form of refunds, to one-and-a-half-million of its customers.
The refunds, which the Commission Chairman, Alan Fels says average about 28-dollars per customer, will go to those who were put on Telstra's Wiring Repair Plan without consent.
Under the plan, which dates back to 1989, householders and businesses with more than one telephone were charged for the repair and upkeep of the extra wiring.
Telstra's managing director of Customer Premises Equipment, Chris Wilkinson, says the company will now review its billing services.
TERMS OF REFERENCE FOR HEALTH INSURANCE INQUIRY
The Federal Government has included an examination of rising health care costs in the terms of reference for the inquiry into private health insurance.
The Government has established the inquiry following recent premium increases that have whittled away the planned health insurance tax rebates due to take effect from next July.
Treasurer, Peter Costello, has asked the Industry Commission to look the structure and efficiency of the health insurance industry including the impact of declining membership levels.
The inquiry will also examine ways funds can be encouraged to offer innovative and affordable health plans to cater for the varying needs of their members.
The commissioners have also been asked to look at increasing health care costs, including the relationship between the health funds and hospitals.
The inquiry will report by the end of February next year.
NEW HAWTHORN BOARD TO BE ANNOUNCED NEXT WEEK
A new board will be appointed to the Hawthorn Football Club in the next week.
Hawthorn directors have formally conceded the vote to merge the club with Melbourne Football Club has been lost.
An interim board will be appointed to Hawthorn next week ... they'll be in place until the club's annual meeting in December.
Vote counting continues and final figures will be announced tomorrow.
